one_sentence: The Born Rule's three irreducible mathematical operations structurally map to the three Persons of the Trinity, each performing a distinct, non-interchangeable role.
executive_summary: This document argues that the Born Rule equation P(a) = |⟨φ|ψ⟩|² contains three irreducible operations—the state vector (|ψ⟩), the measurement basis (⟨φ|), and the modulus squared (|·|²)—that correspond structurally to the three Persons of the Trinity: the Father (possibility space), the Son/Logos (structuring form), and the Spirit (actualization). The mapping is tested across six biblical events (Creation, Fall, Incarnation, Cross, Resurrection, Pentecost) with zero role violations, demonstrating a forced, non-arbitrary isomorphism. The conclusion is that this structural parallel is bidirectional and anti-modalist, requiring simultaneous distinct operations in both physics and theology.
short_summary: This document is a structural isomorphism paper mapping the Born Rule to the Trinity. The core claim is that the three irreducible operations in the Born Rule correspond to the three Persons of the Trinity: Father as possibility space, Son as structuring form, Spirit as actualization. Key evidence includes six biblical events where each Person consistently performs their mapped role without violation. This matters because it suggests a deep structural link between quantum measurement and Trinitarian theology, with implications for both physics and theology.
